name: Keros
overview: Keros is a male member of the tribe of Levi, known specifically as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant indicates his involvement in the religious duties associated with the worship and service of the Lord, as recorded in the book of Ezra. There are no additional personal notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Keros' appears as a proper name in Scripture without any given meaning or special title. It is simply recorded as his personal name in Ezra 2:44.
familyAndRelationships: Keros is identified as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the Levitical lineage responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Keros is significant as one of the Levites who served in the temple, highlighting the restoration of worship following the exile. His mention in Ezra emphasizes the continuity of the Levitical priestly and temple servant roles during the return to Jerusalem. This underscores the faithfulness of God's people in reestablishing proper worship according to the Law.
